questions.q: What does a row in HZ_PARTIES represent?
options: A general ledger journal entry
A supplier's bank account
A customer account with credit terms
A core identity (person, organization, or group) independent of any business relationship
questions.explain: HZ_PARTIES is the party-centric master identity table and carries no financial data or business-relationship detail on its own.

options: HZ_CUST_ACCOUNTS has no connection to HZ_PARTIES
They store identical information
HZ_CUST_ACCOUNTS records the actual customer business relationship (credit terms, account number), separate from the party's core identity
HZ_CUST_ACCOUNTS stores supplier data only
questions.explain: HZ_CUST_ACCOUNTS is the customer account/business-relationship layer, linked back to HZ_PARTIES via PARTY_ID.

questions.q: Why can a single party have more than one customer account?
options: Because a party can have multiple distinct business relationships, like a personal account and a separate business account
Because HZ_PARTIES duplicates itself automatically
Because accounts are randomly generated
It can't — one party means exactly one account
questions.explain: A party can hold several accounts representing different relationships, each with its own account number and terms, all pointing back to the same party.

options: The party's legal name
The business purpose of a customer account site, such as bill-to or ship-to
The supplier's purchasing site flag
The general ledger period status
questions.explain: HZ_CUST_SITE_USES_ALL captures what a given account site is used for (bill-to, ship-to, or both), often carrying its own attributes like payment terms.

questions.q: Why does Oracle model party, account, site, and site-use as separate layers instead of one flat customer table?
options: Because flat tables are not supported in Oracle databases
It has no practical benefit
To make queries harder on purpose
Because real business relationships don't fit a flat shape — the same entity can be both customer and supplier, hold multiple accounts, and reuse addresses for different purposes
questions.explain: Separating identity, account, site, and site-use avoids duplicating identity data every time a new relationship, account, or location is added.
